INCIDENTBOT: :rotating_light: Alert: abnormal authentication patterns detected for multiple service tokens and evidence of public access to archived audit files. Paging @oncall-auth and @security. Please acknowledge.

maria: ack. Seeing a burst starting ~03:05 UTC with many 401s and some 200s on S3 GETs for audit-archive-v2. Client id shows svc-ingest-collector.

sam: found a handful of GETs from 45.83.10.22 and 45.83.10.23 to s3://redwood-audit-archive-v2/2026-03-15/*.log with 'x-amz-acl: public-read' set in the object metadata. These objects were created by a nightly job.

raj: initial hypothesis: a debug deploy added header dumping and an automated job applied an ACL change via a mis-scoped role. Immediate steps: 1) revoke tokens for svc-ingest-collector, 2) restrict bucket to deny public access, 3) block the suspicious IPs at the edge, 4) collect potentially exposed objects for forensics. I'll coordinate rotations.

tim: I'm on rotations and firewall. Will create short-lived replacement keys and remove old ones from vault. Also rolling back the debug deploy that changed logging.

maria: logs indicate token replay attempts where the same bearer token is used with different IPs. Could be credential stuffing from scraped logs.\n
opsbot: Task queued: revoke-service-token svc-ingest-collector (initiated by tim). ETA 90s.

deploy-bot: Noted: initiating rollback of commit sha: b4c3f2 that introduced verbose header logging to auth-service. Rolling back to previous stable.

sam: policy update applied to bucket redwood-audit-archive-v2 to disable ACLs and enforce `BlockPublicAcls`. Change event id: bucket-policy-20260315-0312. Also removed lifecycle that was changing ACLs.

emily: running a content scan on suspect objects for token patterns and PII. So far found 5 files with header dumps containing fragments that look like bearer tokens (not full length). Staging them in a forensic bucket s3://redwood-forensics/1954332000/ (private).

jessie: support triage: early telemetry shows an uptick in 401s for customers acct-501 and acct-702 during the incident window. We're preparing a short advisory template but holding until scope confirmed.

maria: after rollback, auth-service logs no longer emit headers. Auth failure rates trending down.

raj: rotation progress: rotated svc-ingest-collector token, rotated related helper svc-collector-helper token, revoked old tokens in IAM, updated secrets in k8s and vault. Please confirm downstream consumers refreshed keys.

tim: updated runtime envs and triggered secrets refresh. Notifying teams via #eng and tagging owners.

opsbot: Revoke complete. Old tokens invalidated.

legal-bot: If forensic scan identifies any customer PII, escalate to privacy@redwood.com and open privacy incident with severity per policy. Keep an audit trail of all access.

emily: scan results: no PII found. Token fragments may have been truncated and likely insufficient for unauthorized access, but given replay attempts we treated them as compromised and rotated anyway.

raj: good call. Next steps: 1) perform an inventory of all jobs that write to audit buckets and add logging hygiene checks, 2) tighten S3 bucket policy to deny ACL changes from non-admin roles, 3) run a global token usage audit to detect any other tokens with similar characteristics. I'll own the inventory item.

jessie: drafting customer advisory now. Will state what we know, mitigations taken (rotations, bucket lockdown, rollback), and recommended customer actions (rotate their own ingestion credentials if they use customer-managed tokens).

maria: handoff to oncall-auth for follow-up post-rotate validation and to write the postmortem. @oncall-auth please verify token usage logs for any signs of successful data exfil beyond the S3 GETs we saw.

oncall-auth: acknowledged. We'll run full query across token logs and share results in the postmortem thread.

INCIDENTBOT: Incident declared mitigated. Please open a postmortem at #postmortems/inc-1954332000 and attach timeline, root cause, and action items.

jessie: customer advisory scheduled to go out at 03:50 UTC unless legal requests changes.

maria: note for postmortem: root cause = accidental header-logging regression in auth-service + mis-scoped lifecycle job that set public ACLs on archived logs. Mitigations = rollback, token rotations, bucket policy enforcement, WAF blocks.

tim: add to action items: add automated check to CI that prevents commits that modify logger settings to include headers; enforce S3 ACL restrictions via terraform policy; rotate any tokens that were created within the same deployment window.

raj: I'll run the broader token audit and follow up with a list of any additional services needing rotation by EOD.

jessie: marking incident P1 (security exposure) and assigning the postmortem owner to raj and maria. Closing thread; moving any new updates to the postmortem doc. :lock:
